Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Church life

confession noun

the sacrament

also go to confession, penance, the sacrament of confession, confess one’s sins

late Latin

Vulg. 1 Jo. 1.9
M-O s.v. confession; hear confessions (Tursellinus, 1652)

cōnfessiō, cōnfessiōnis f.

noun, third declension

confession (of sins)

Classically an admission; in the Church the confession of sins, and the sacrament itself, which both churches keep: the Greek and Slavonic churches also call it the mystery of repentance (μετάνοια), the Latin Church the sacrament of penance (paenitentia). To confess is peccāta cōnfitērī; to hear confessions, cōnfessiōnēs audīre (Morgan–Owens).

Other words

  • exomologēsis, exomologēsis f. — confession

    noun, third declension · also used · late Latin · Tert. Paen. 9 (Lewis & Short)

    Tertullian’s Greek word, ἐξομολόγησις, for the confession made in penance.

Examples

  • Sī cōnfiteāmur peccāta nostra: fidēlis est, et jūstus, ut remittat nōbīs peccāta nostra

    If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sinsVulg. 1 Jo. 1.9

  • Cōnfitēminī ergō alterutrum peccāta vestra, et ōrāte prō invicem ut salvēminī

    So confess your sins to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healedVulg. Jac. 5.16

See also confession, sin, repent, forgive, forgiveness, priest.

SourcesLewis & Short: confessio · Lewis & Short: confiteor · Lewis & Short: exomologesis
